h: Guarding Spiritual Greatness Through Living Words of Torah

p: with the rebuke of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and so too the haftarah of "Chazon."
so why did they not institute
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
according to what is written in the Midrash Rabbah
one saw her in her tranquility,
one saw her in her recklessness,
and one saw her in her disgrace.
in their glory and their tranquility
it added the expression "in their glory,"
which was not said in the parable.
לֹא רַק עַל שִׁיוּוּי הַלָּשׁוֹן אֵיכָה
it was not only the sameness of the word "Eichah"
meaning: How has such a thing come about?
And this is the matter of Moshe's rebuke:
when he saw Yisrael "in their glory,"
and "in their tranquility" in this world;
at the beginning of the parshah (Devarim 1:6):
"Hashem our God spoke to us at Chorev:
you have inherited at this mountain"
means that you are at a great level,
and the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
"And I said to you at that time, saying:
Now the two words "at that time"
also there is a dispute among the Rishonim
as to when the appointment of the Sanhedrin was.
"And I said to you at that time"
and you were ready to enter Eretz Yisrael,
the holiness of Torah she'b'al peh
that it was able to enter
And likewise at the Giving of the Torah,
when with the utterance "You shall have no"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts,
it afterward returned to its place
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי, א, ב)
(as is written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah on "Let him kiss me," 1:2).
And therefore "I cannot by myself alone
so that there be fixed in you
And he said: "Hashem your God has multiplied you"
like the stars of the heavens," etc.
and it is the great level
they rise up to the stars."
"May Hashem, the God of your fathers,
your burden, your load and your strife?"
there are among you troublesome ones,
(as is written in the Sifrei, brought in Rashi);
for even among the great ones of the world
when there is a personal interest
were it not for Hashem who stood by them
that the study of Torah be implanted
לְכָךְ הָבוּ לָכֶם אֲנָשִׁים וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם א, יג)
that each one will be known,
and likewise he will know his people,
and will be better able to have an effect
that the words of Torah be fixed in them.
"And I will place them as your heads":
(as is written in the Sifrei and Midrash Rabbah);
וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן
and to instill the words of Torah
And this will be through the power
that Moshe Rabbeinu would give to the judges,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם א, טז)
that he gave them power "to say,"
that they would instill it in the heart
of all the people particular to each.
From whom is it fitting to learn Torah
from you or from your disciple?" etc.
And this is why it says "And you answered me":
that the answer was against me.
that "osi" is written without a vav:
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
like Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן יג וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
(as is written in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 13 and elsewhere);
אַךְ הָיָה עַל יְדֵי פִּיתּוּי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
But it was through the enticement of the yetzer hara
(as is written in Rashi's commentary from the Sifrei).
And all this is a preface
to inherit the power of Torah she'b'al peh,
that the words of Torah be fixed
And this is the intent of the Midrash:
in the affairs of this world;
How has such a thing come about,
that at such a great level
the yetzer hara can still enter?
that the words of Torah be fixed in their hearts
And this is the connection of Parshas Devarim
for these are the words of the first groomsman,
while they were at their level,
that they not come, chas v'shalom,
to what they came to afterward,
when Yeshayahu saw them in their recklessness
And through the reading of Parshas Devarim
one merits that the words of Torah be fixed in the heart,
and to repair at the root
that Yeshayahu lamented over their recklessness,
and to merit that there be rectified
the "Eichah" of Yirmiyahu over their disgrace;
and it be transformed into joy and gladness

Repairing the Three Laments at Their Root
